title: MIRACLE: Multimodal Information Retrieval via a Combined In-Memory Processing and Content Addressable Memory Approach
problem: Multimodal retrieval via neural feature extraction + similarity search is inefficient; cosine similarity on von Neumann wastes memory bandwidth, and pure hashing sacrifices accuracy due to modal heterogeneity.
motivation: Transformer-based feature extraction is well-accelerated, but retrieval remains under-optimized; energy-efficient retrieval is critical for real-time multimodal systems.
method: Hybrid architecture combining in-memory random hashing (PIM) for fast approximate ranking and content-addressable memory (CAM) for parallel search space reduction, followed by final cosine reranking for accuracy recovery.
key_novelty: PIM+CAM hybrid that leverages device-intrinsic hashing properties in memory while using CAM for efficient search reduction.
contributions: PIM-based in-memory random hashing for multimodal features
Cosine similarity reranking for accuracy restoration
9.45x latency and 30.20x energy improvement over CPU baseline
limitations: Not discussed; limited to vision+text modalities, scalability to higher-dimensional embeddings unclear.
primary_theme: PIM+CAM hybrid for multimodal vector retrieval
